data.title: Solo Bitcoin Miner Finds Block 966351 and Earns 3.147 BTC Reward
data.description:
A Bitcoin solo miner using Braiins Solo mined block 966351 and received the full 3.147 BTC block reward. According to ChainCatcher, this was the first successful solo block on the Bitcoin network in nearly 40 days.

The previous solo mining success occurred on August 2, when a miner using Solo CKPool earned a 3.1569 BTC reward. Foundry, Antpool, F2Pool, ViaBTC, and Spiderpool currently control about 78.31% of Bitcoin network hash power, making solo block discovery relatively unlikely.

data.title: STOCKS | Trump Surgeon General Pick Holds Stakes in Tobacco and Beverage Stocks
data.description:
Financial disclosure documents released on Thursday showed that Nicole Saphier, U.S. President Donald Trump's nominee for Surgeon General, holds investments in Philip Morris International, as well as beverage companies including Monster Beverage, Coca-Cola, and PepsiCo. According to Sina Finance, she disclosed the holdings in an ethics agreement and said she would divest all or part of the positions, while also selling shares in several major pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, including Eli Lilly, Biogen, Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer, AstraZeneca, Merck, and AbbVie.

U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has made cracking down on unhealthy ultra-processed foods a work priority. According to Sina Finance, Saphier also supports removing food additives, reducing ultra-processed foods in the diet, and encouraging exercise.

Saphier is the founder of DropRx, which sells “physician-formulated” herbal dietary supplements. According to Sina Finance, she also serves as breast imaging director at the Monmouth branch of Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New Jersey and was previously a Fox News commentator.

The Surgeon General is known as America’s top doctor and is responsible for delivering authoritative scientific information to the public and guiding healthier behavior. According to Sina Finance, Saphier's Senate confirmation hearing is scheduled for September 16 (Wednesday).

data.title: STOCKS | Huatai Securities Says U.S. CPI Beat Makes a September Rate Hike a Must
data.description: According to Jin10, Huatai Securities said August core inflation rose more than expected on a month-on-month basis, making a September Federal Reserve rate hike a "must" and increasing the credibility risk of not hiking in September. The report said August nonfarm payrolls also beat expectations, Middle East tensions pushed oil prices above $100, and August CPI became the key variable in market pricing of whether the Fed will hike in September. It added that core inflation in August accelerated more than expected, while the core services ex-housing component watched by the Fed did not show further signs of slowing. The report also said low inventories, concerns over surging oil prices, AI-driven price increases passing through to downstream sectors, and a new round of local tariffs could all disrupt the pace of U.S. disinflation. Looking ahead, the report said CPI data may push neutral voter Christopher Waller to turn hawkish at the September FOMC meeting, reducing internal Fed resistance to a September hike. It added that August data also cleared obstacles for a rate hike, and if Kevin Warsh fails to deliver on his hawkish pledge from the August Jackson Hole meeting in September, the Fed's credibility will face a greater challenge and long-term U.S. Treasury yields will be harder to control.

data.title: Larry Ellison Enters Trading Plan To Sell Up To $7.5 Billion Of Oracle Stock
data.description: According to CNBC, Oracle founder Larry Ellison has entered into a trading plan that would allow him to sell up to 50 million shares of the software company, worth about $7.5 billion at current prices. Ellison adopted the plan on June 22, and it is set to end on Oct. 24, according to a regulatory filing published Friday. He controls more than 40% of Oracle, according to FactSet, and would still own 1.1 billion shares if he sells all of the stock covered by the plan. Since the start of this century, Ellison has never sold more than 25,000 Oracle shares at any one time, according to FactSet. Oracle said in its earnings report on Thursday that it beat estimates and posted 121% year-over-year growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

data.title: STOCKS | Boeing Submits Final Contract Offer to Engineers Union With 10% Raise
data.description:
Boeing has submitted a final contract proposal to the Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace, or SPEEA, according to the latest information posted on Boeing's website. According to Sina Finance, if approved, the proposal would include a guaranteed 10% pay increase, followed by another 4% increase in March 2027.

Boeing said the union bargaining team recommended that members vote in favor. The contract also includes a pay pool, with annual increases of 6% in 2028, 2029, and 2030, and a guaranteed minimum annual raise of at least 4% in each of those three years.

data.title: ASIA NIGHT SESSION | Nikkei, Taiwan Futures Rebound Overnight as U.S. Stocks Snap Losing Streak; Hang Seng Futures Flat
data.description:
According to HKET, RTHK and Yahoo Taiwan, Asian index futures firmed in overnight trading after U.S. equities rebounded, ending a four-session slide, as oil prices eased and an in-line August U.S. CPI reading hardened expectations for a Federal Reserve rate increase. The Dow rose 509.19 points, or 0.98%, to 52,573.29.

Nikkei 225 futures recovered in the Osaka overnight session. The near-month December 2026 contract closed the night session at 64,510, up 550 points, per JPX official data, rebounding from the Tokyo cash market's near-2% loss earlier Friday.

Hong Kong futures were little changed overnight, with the Hang Seng Index night futures ending 6 points lower at 24,793 and the H-share night index up 0.4% at 5,811. Among ADRs converted to Hong Kong dollars, the HSBC ADR traded about 1.17% above its Hong Kong close, while the Tencent ADR was down 0.31%, the Meituan ADR down 0.51% and Alibaba's U.S. shares off 0.30%. The Hang Seng cash market had closed Friday down 148 points at 24,805.

Taiwan futures led the overnight advance, with the TAIEX night futures settling at 46,588, up 401 points or 0.87%, buoyed by a 1.22% gain in the TSMC ADR. The TAIEX cash index had closed Friday down 755 points, or 1.61%, at 46,184.

data.title: US MARKET CLOSE | Three Major Indexes Rise as Sticky CPI Lifts Fed Rate-Hike Bets to 87%; Oil Retreats
data.description: US stocks closed higher on Friday as investors digested the Consumer Price Index (CPI) data, which showed inflation remained sticky and reinforced market bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike next week, according to Sina Finance. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 509.19 points, or 0.98%, to 52,573.29; the S&P 500 gained 65.28 points, or 0.86%, to 7,656.98; and the Nasdaq added 251.32 points, or 0.96%, to 26,333.04. Most of the "Magnificent Seven" advanced, with Google, Amazon and Apple up more than 1%, Meta, Microsoft and Tesla posting modest gains, and Nvidia slightly lower. Among large-cap technology stocks, Dell Technologies surged more than 11%, Super Micro Computer rose more than 7%, Qualcomm gained nearly 3%, and Intel and SpaceX climbed more than 2%. Optical communications names advanced, with Marvell Technology up more than 4% and Coherent up more than 4%. Storage stocks were mixed, as Seagate Technology fell more than 3%, SanDisk dropped more than 3%, Western Digital declined nearly 3%, and SK Hynix rose nearly 1%. The three major averages had previously fallen for four consecutive trading days; for the Dow, that marked the longest daily losing streak since late April. Oil prices retreated, giving back part of the gains recorded this week on escalating Middle East tensions. At the close, New York Mercantile Exchange light crude for October delivery fell $2.43 to settle at $100.05 per barrel, down 2.37%, while London Brent crude for November delivery fell $3.02 to settle at $104.61 per barrel, down 2.81%. Even so, WTI crude rose nearly 10% for the week and Brent gained nearly 9%. The latest US inflation data showed rising energy prices exerted upward pressure on consumer goods. The August CPI rose 0.4% month-over-month and 3.4% year-over-year, in line with Dow Jones expectations, while core CPI, excluding energy and food, rose 0.3% month-over-month, slightly above expectations. The report prompted traders to increase bets on a Fed rate hike this month. According to the CME FedWatch tool, the market now prices the probability of a 25-basis-point hike at next week's FOMC meeting at about 87%, up from 72% the prior day and 50% a week earlier. After the report, yields were broadly steady, but the 2-year Treasury yield broke above 4.6%, reaching its highest level since July 2024. Seema Shah, chief global strategist at Principal Asset Management, said the debate has shifted quickly from whether the Fed will hike to the more important question of how many hikes this cycle will ultimately require, adding that policymakers may conclude more than one hike is needed to rebuild price stability after five straight years of above-target inflation.
